title: Job 15
paragraphs: ¹ Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: ² "Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill himself up with the east wind? ³ Should he argue with useless talk, with words that do no good? ⁴ But you are undermining the fear of God and hindering devotion before him. ⁵ Your own guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

⁶ Your own mouth condemns you, not I — your own lips testify against you. ⁷ Were you the first person ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills? ⁸ Were you listening in on God's council? Do you have a monopoly on wisdom? ⁹ What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not understand? ¹⁰ Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us — men older even than your father.

¹¹ Are God's consolations not enough for you? Is the word spoken gently to you not sufficient? ¹² Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash, ¹³ so that you turn your spirit against God and let such words pour from your mouth? ¹⁴ What is a mortal, that they should be clean? What is one born of woman, that they should be righteous? ¹⁵ If God puts no trust even in his holy ones, and even the heavens are not pure in his sight,

¹⁶ how much more corrupt and depraved is a person who drinks in evil like water! ¹⁷ I will show you — listen to me — and I will tell you what I have seen; ¹⁸ what wise men have declared without hiding, passed down from their fathers, ¹⁹ to whom the land was given while no stranger moved among them. ²⁰ The wicked are in torment all their days, and the years that have been stored up for the ruthless are few.

²¹ Terrifying sounds fill their ears; in the midst of peace, the destroyer comes upon them. ²² They do not believe they will return from darkness, and they are destined for the sword. ²³ They wander about, asking, "Where can I find bread?" — knowing that a day of darkness is ready at hand. ²⁴ Distress and anguish terrify them; they overpower them, like a king ready for battle.

²⁵ Because they have stretched out their hand against God and defied the Almighty, ²⁶ charging at him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of their shields — ²⁷ because they covered their face with fat and made their waist thick with flesh, ²⁸ they live in desolate cities, in houses that no one else inhabits, houses crumbling into ruins. ²⁹ They will no longer be rich; their wealth will not endure, and their possessions will not spread over the earth. ³⁰ They will not escape the darkness; flames will wither their shoots, and they will depart by the breath of God's mouth.

³¹ Let them not trust in emptiness and deceive themselves — emptiness will be their reward. ³² Their branch will wither before its time, and their shoots will not be green. ³³ They will be like a vine that shakes off its unripe grapes, like an olive tree casting off its blossoms. ³⁴ For the company of the godless will produce nothing, and fire will consume the tents of those who take bribes. ³⁵ They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb brings forth deception."
